title: Exploration and Exploitation in Organizational Learning
authors: James G. March
pdf_note: JSTOR cover page precedes the article.
rationale: Mutual-learning and competition-for-primacy models; all six figures are simulation output with m=30, n=50, 80 iterations and p1-p4 values stated in text and captions.

title: Organizational Learning and Personnel Turnover
authors: Kathleen Carley
rationale: Monte Carlo model of teams and hierarchies learning under turnover; decision rule, task sizes, turnover rates, 400 runs of 2500 periods all stated. C program only on request.

title: An Organizational Learning Model of Convergence and Reorientation
authors: Theresa K. Lant; Stephen J. Mezias
rationale: Computer simulation of 150 learning organizations over 50 periods, 50 runs. The appendix gives the search, aspiration and change rules with parameter values.

title: Social Network Effects on the Extent of Innovation Diffusion: A Computer Simulation
authors: Eric Abrahamson; Lori Rosenkopf
rationale: Threshold diffusion model on a simulated core-periphery network. Network size, link generation, profit distribution, ambiguity levels and trial counts are all given; regressions use simulated data.

title: Training and Turnover in the Evolution of Organizations
authors: Natalie S. Glance; Tad Hogg; Bernardo A. Huberman
pdf_note: Page 1 is a JSTOR cover page.
rationale: Agent-based model of training and turnover. Figures 1-6 come from computer experiments. The appendix gives the algorithm, parameter values and initial conditions.

title: A Chaotic Model of Innovative Search: Some Answers, Many Questions
authors: Kenneth W. Koput
rationale: Chaotic difference-equation model simulated in MATLAB with parameters drawn from printed ranges. The empirical TAP series and estimates are excerpted from Koput (1992), not reanalysed.

title: Organization Culture as a Complex System: Balance and Information in Models of Influence and Selection
authors: Kenneth A. Frank; Kyle Fahrbach
rationale: Influence and selection models are given as equations with starting values and parameters for each run; Figures 1, 2, 4 and 6 to 9 are simulated, no empirical data.

title: Avoiding Complexity Catastrophe in Coevolutionary Pockets: Strategies for Rugged Landscapes
authors: Bill McKelvey
rationale: Translates Kauffman's NK[C] model to firms. Every finding is Kauffman's (1993) and Figure 2 is reproduced from his book. The author runs no simulation.

title: Path Dependence, Competition, and Succession in the Dynamics of Scientific Revolution
authors: John D. Sterman; Jason Wittenberg
rationale: System dynamics model of competing paradigms. The paper gives an overview, causal diagrams and one equation; complete documentation is available only from the authors.

title: Extending the Cyert-March Duopoly Model: Organizational and Economic Insights
authors: Michael J. Prietula; Harry S. Watson
rationale: Computational Cyert-March duopoly model, 78 simulations. Appendix gives only the three manipulated routines; other parameters defer to Cyert and March (1963); algorithm available from first author.

title: Adaptation as Information Restriction: The Hot Stove Effect
authors: Jerker Denrell; James G. March
pdf_note: Last PDF page carries no article text.
rationale: Stochastic learning and competitive selection models; Figures 1-6 and Tables 1a-1b are simulation averages with equations and all parameter values given in text and captions.

title: Reproducing Knowledge: Replication Without Imitation at Moderate Complexity
authors: Jan W. Rivkin
rationale: NK simulation of replicator and imitator search. Tables 3-6 give N = 12, K, r, i, theta and 100-200 landscapes; search rules are described in Section 3.

title: A Simulation-Based Approach to Understanding the Dynamics of Innovation Implementation
authors: Nelson P. Repenning
package_where: web.mit.edu/nelsonr/www/implementation.html: technical appendix with full model documentation and a running Vensim model (endnotes 1-3). URL as printed in 2002.
rationale: System dynamics model in Vensim. Functional forms and the extended model's parameters sit in a technical appendix posted on the author's MIT page, not in the article.

title: Vicarious Learning, Undersampling of Failure, and the Myths of Management
authors: Jerker Denrell
rationale: Stochastic selection model with closed-form expectations and Monte Carlo runs (50,000 simulations); Figures 2-6 are numerical. No empirical data. Distributions and parameter values stated in text.

title: Temporarily Divide to Conquer: Centralized, Decentralized, and Reintegrated Organizational Approaches to Exploration and Adaptation
authors: Nicolaj Siggelkow; Daniel A. Levinthal
rationale: Agent-based NK simulation; every result is a performance average over 10,000 generated landscapes. N, K, structures and reintegration periods are stated.

title: Unanimity Rule and Organizational Decision Making: A Simulation Model
authors: A. Georges L. Romme
rationale: System dynamics model in Ithink; Figures 3-7 are model output. Equations are printed, but constants and full documentation are only available on request from the author.

title: Cognition and Hierarchy: Rethinking the Microfoundations of Capabilities’ Development
authors: Giovanni Gavetti
rationale: NK-type simulation of cognition and hierarchy. Parameters are given, but the three stored representations and some regime mechanics are described only loosely.

title: When the Market Misleads: Stock Prices, Firm Behavior, and Industry Evolution
authors: Carl Joachim Kock
rationale: Figures 1-6 come from a Cournot duopoly learning simulation. The appendix gives the algorithm but not the values of demand, costs, investment or discount rate. The brokerage case only motivates.

title: Speed and Search: Designing Organizations for Turbulence and Complexity
authors: Nicolaj Siggelkow; Jan W. Rivkin
rationale: Agent-based NK simulation of organizational search; all results in Tables 3-7 come from the model, with parameters stated in text and table notes.

title: How Much Better Are the Most-Prestigious Journals? The Statistics of Academic Publication
authors: William H. Starbuck
rationale: Main results come from a simulated statistical model of peer review. Figures 1-2 and Tables 6-7 also use ISI impact factors (subscription). Later model steps described only verbally.

title: Innovators, Imitators, and the Evolving Architecture of Problem-Solving Networks
authors: Myong-Hun Chang; Joseph E. Harrington
rationale: Agent-based model with EWA reinforcement learning. Table 1 lists every parameter value; horizon (15,000 periods), 100 replications and steady-state window are stated. Figures 2-13 report results.

title: Information Technology and Organizational Learning: An Investigation of Exploration and Exploitation Processes
authors: Gerald C. Kane; Maryam Alavi
rationale: Extends March's (1991) computational model; Figures 1-6 all come from simulation runs. Company Z case evidence only shapes the model design.

title: Two Faces of Search: Alternative Generation and Alternative Evaluation
authors: Thorbjørn Knudsen; Daniel A. Levinthal
rationale: NK landscape simulation (N=10, K=3 baseline) with linear screening functions and six organizational forms whose polynomials are printed in the appendix. No data.

title: The Value of Moderate Obsession: Insights from a New Model of Organizational Search
authors: Sidney G. Winter; Gino Cattani; Alex Dorsch
rationale: Fractal-landscape search simulation; all results computed. Table 1 and the appendix give parameters, but the landscape height-scaling regression is not reported.

title: Near-Term Liability of Exploitation: Exploration and Exploitation in Multistage Problems
authors: Christina Fang; Daniel Levinthal
rationale: Q-learning simulation on a two-peak landscape. N, payoffs, learning weights and temperatures are given; peak locations, start positions and episode limits are not stated.

title: Is the Resource-Based View a Practical Organizational Theory?
authors: Richard J. Arend; Moren Lévesque
rationale: Simulated Cournot industry with regressions run on simulated data. Table 1 gives parameters, but the VRIO acquisition cost and imitation probability come from unreported runs.

title: How Much to Copy? Determinants of Effective Imitation Breadth
authors: Felipe A. Csaszar; Nicolaj Siggelkow
rationale: NK simulation of imitation breadth; N=12, M=5, K and S values and 1,000 runs stated. Figures 1-9 numerical; online appendix holds robustness only.

title: Balancing Exploration and Exploitation Through Structural Design: The Isolation of Subgroups and Organizational Learning
authors: Christina Fang; Jeho Lee; Melissa A. Schilling
rationale: Agent-based extension of March (1991) on a rewired connected-caveman network. Appendix B lists every parameter and the simulation steps.

title: Getting There: Exploring the Role of Expectations and Preproduction Delays in Processes of Organizational Founding
authors: Alessandro Lomi; Erik R. Larsen; Filippo Carlo Wezel
rationale: System dynamics model run in Vensim; Poisson regressions use simulated founding counts. Table 2 reprints published estimates. The appendix gives parameter ranges, not every base-case value.

title: A General Framework for Estimating Multidimensional Contingency Fit
authors: Simon C. Parker; Arjen van Witteloostuijn
rationale: Methods paper. Tables 3 to 6 come from regressions on randomly generated data under stated DGPs (equations 7 and 8). The Table 6 sample-size criterion is not defined.

title: Investing in Capabilities: The Dynamics of Resource Allocation
authors: Corinne A. Coen; Catherine A. Maritan
rationale: Agent-based Swarm model of three firms choosing investment projects. Figures 2-8 are averages of 100 runs. Budget renewal amounts and the random draws' distributions aren't stated.

title: Dynamic Resource Capabilities: Managing Workforce Knowledge with a Technology Upgrade
authors: Cheryl Gaimon; Gülru F. Özkan; Karen Napoleon
rationale: Optimal control model solved analytically (Theorems 1-6). No numerical experiments; note 6 says figures are illustrative only.

title: Understanding the Role of Worker Interdependence in Team Selection
authors: William P. Millhiser; Corinne A. Coen; Daniel Solow
rationale: Computational simulation of team-assignment policies on random interdependence matrices; Figures 2-5 are simulated. Performance rule and N, K given, number of runs not stated.

title: Learning, Imitation, and the Use of Knowledge: A Comparison of Markets, Hierarchies, and Teams
authors: John C. Butler; Jovan Grahovac
rationale: Agent-based simulation of markets, teams and hierarchies; rules in prose, parameters in Table 1; results in Figures 4-6 and Table 2. VBA code only on request.

title: Entrepreneurial Success and Failure: Confidence and Fallible Judgment
authors: Robin M. Hogarth; Natalia Karelaia
rationale: Analytical threshold model illustrated by Monte Carlo: 5,000 populations of 100 individuals, normal draws with stated means, variances and success cutoffs. No data.

title: How to Get What You Want When You Do Not Know What You Want: A Model of Incentives, Organizational Structure, and Learning
authors: Luigi Marengo; Corrado Pasquali
rationale: Simulated decision processes on random policy landscapes, n = 8, 1,000 repetitions (Tables 3-6). Paper gives only a summary account; details and code on request.

title: Impact of Growth Opportunities and Competition on Firm-Level Capability Development Trade-offs
authors: Hazhir Rahmandad
package_where: Electronic companion S4 (Vensim models), online version at http://orgsci.journal.informs.org/
rationale: System dynamics simulation of capability investment. Equations 1 to 18 and Table 1 give the model and parameters; Vensim models are in the electronic companion.

title: Dealing with Complexity: Integrated vs. Chunky Search Processes
authors: Oliver Baumann; Nicolaj Siggelkow
rationale: NK simulation (N=8, K=7, 10,000 landscapes); search rule, search domains and expansion patterns are fully described; every table and figure is computed from the model.

title: An Efficient Frontier in Organization Design: Organizational Structure as a Determinant of Exploration and Exploitation
authors: Felipe A. Csaszar
rationale: Mathematical model of organizational screening; Figures 6-12 plot computed omission and commission errors for enumerated organizations. Equations, algorithm and distributions in Appendices A-C.

title: In the Short Term We Divide, in the Long Term We Unite: Demographic Crisscrossing and the Effects of Faultlines on Subgroup Polarization
authors: Michael Mäs; Andreas Flache; Károly Takács; Karen A. Jehn
rationale: Agent-based model of opinion and network dynamics in teams; Figures 3-9 come from computational experiments with stated parameters. Online appendix holds robustness only.

title: Rationalizing Organizational Change: A Need for Comparative Testing
authors: Arkadiy V. Sakhartov; Timothy B. Folta
rationale: Regressions on simulated agents, no real data. Rational-choice simulation is specified in text and endnotes; satisficing and mixed-behavior simulations are explained only in Online Appendices B and C.

title: Diffusion as Classification
authors: Dror Etzion
rationale: Agent-based diffusion model run in Vensim; Figures 5-10 are model output. Equations and Table 1 parameters given, but T and extension parameters are not; code on request only.

title: Memory and Organizational Evolvability in a Neutral Landscape
authors: Amit Jain; Bruce Kogut
rationale: NK simulation with neutrality and memory. Parameters stated (N=10, K=2-8, Ne=0.10, memory 25, 100 runs, 250 periods) but drift, memory replacement and recall-error rules are only described in prose.

title: A Model of Collective Interpretation
authors: Giovanni Gavetti; Massimo Warglien
rationale: Multiagent Hopfield-network simulation; Figures 7-10 report runs. Grid values are given, but the stored prototypes and update order are not fully listed.

title: Three Facets of Organizational Adaptation: Selection, Variety, and Plasticity
authors: Daniel A. Levinthal; Alessandro Marino
rationale: NK-landscape computational model of templates, plasticity and internal selection. Figures 2-3 and Table 1 come from 250 runs of 1,000 steps. All parameter values stated. No code posted.

title: Organizational Obsolescence, Drifting Tastes, and Age Dependence in Organizational Life Chances
authors: Gaël Le Mens; Michael T. Hannan; László Pólos
sources: Data on microbreweries and brewpubs assembled by Carroll and Swaminathan (2000) [T4, sample]
special_software: Custom maximum simulated likelihood estimator for a random-walk failure model with absorbing barrier (Le Mens et al. 2011)
rationale: Logic-based theory with theorems plus one estimated table on Carroll and Swaminathan's brewery data, which other researchers assembled and no archive holds.

title: Great Vessels Take a Long Time to Mature: Early Success Traps and Competences in Exploitation and Exploration
authors: Mooweon Rhee; Tohyun Kim
rationale: Agent-based learning model coded in Java; equations and Table 1 give every base parameter; results are Figures 1-3, averaged over 5,000 Monte Carlo iterations.

title: Tipping Points: The Gender Segregating and Desegregating Effects of Network Recruitment
authors: Brian Rubineau; Roberto M. Fernandez
rationale: Markov population model with closed-form equilibria; Figures 2-5 plot them over stated parameter ranges. Table 1 applies the formulas to three firm cases whose inputs are printed.

title: Organizational Adaptation in Offshoring: The Relative Performance of Home- and Host-Based Learning Strategies
authors: Christian Geisler Asmussen; Marcus M. Larsen; Torben Pedersen
package_where: Online Appendix 4 (Excel VBA code), journal supplement at http://dx.doi.org/10.1287/orsc.2016.1060
rationale: Simulation of home- vs host-based learning on a modular landscape. Tables 1-2 and Figures 2-3 are model output. Nokia case is illustrative only. VBA code in Online Appendix 4.

title: How Initial Representations Shape Coupled Learning Processes
authors: Phanish Puranam; Murali Swamy
rationale: Agent-based reinforcement-learning model. Equations 1-3 and m, p, payoffs, tau, learning rates, 5,000 pairs and 100 trials are stated. Only the proofs of Propositions 1-2 are online.

title: Inertia in Routines: A Hidden Source of Organizational Variation
authors: Sangyoon Yi; Thorbjørn Knudsen; Markus C. Becker
rationale: NK model of routines with implementation delay R and endogenous change E; N, K, runs given, but handling of pending plans is prose only and no code is posted.

title: Experiential Learning, Competitive Selection, and Downside Risk: A New Perspective on Managerial Risk Taking
authors: Johannes G. Jaspersen; Richard Peter
rationale: Simulations of aspiration-based learning and competitive selection. Update rules, the quadratic-normal lottery construction, population sizes, rounds and Table 1 defaults are all printed.

title: The Impact of Learning and Overconfidence on Entrepreneurial Entry and Exit
authors: John S. Chen; David C. Croson; Daniel W. Elfenbein; Hart E. Posen
rationale: Computational learning model with all parameter values given. The exit threshold and option value formulas are left to Ryan and Lippman (2003), and no time step is stated.

title: When Two Bosses Are Better Than One: Nearly Decomposable Systems and Organizational Adaptation
authors: Daniel A. Levinthal; Maciej Workiewicz
rationale: Agent-based NK-type model, results in Figures 4 and 5. Parameters are in the text, but the detailed search algorithm is in online appendix A1.

title: Does the Middle Conform or Compete? Quality Thresholds Predict the Locus of Innovation
authors: Anthony Vashevko
rationale: Formal threshold model with computed figures and multi-period simulation. Utility, risk parameters and actor count given; reward size and number of runs are not.

title: A Contingency Theory of Representational Complexity in Organizations
authors: Felipe A. Csaszar; James Ostler
package_where: Simulation code in the online appendix, https://doi.org/10.1287/orsc.2019.1346
rationale: Performance is computed by simulating a Brunswik lens screening model. Section 3 gives the algorithm and all parameter values. Code is said to be in the online appendix.

title: Focus in Searching Core–Periphery Structures
authors: Dirk Martignoni; Thomas Keil; Markus Lang
rationale: NK model with core-periphery interaction matrices and focused local search. N=16, p=2/3, 200,000 runs, K values per structure in figure notes; all results simulated.

title: If Higher Pay Is Profitable, Why Is It So Rare? Modeling Competing Strategies in Mass Market Services
authors: Hazhir Rahmandad; Zeynep Ton
rationale: System dynamics model motivated by case studies; results in Figures 2-4 come from the model. Full equations and parameter values are in Online Appendices A1-A2, not the PDF.

title: Architectural Search and Innovation
authors: Daniel Albert; Nicolaj Siggelkow
rationale: NK-landscape simulation of architectural search. N = 12, initial complexity levels, scope levels, 500 runs and 200 or 10,000 periods are given; Section 3 describes search and acceptance rules.

title: From Lock-In to Transformation: A Path-Centric Theory of Emerging Technology and Organizing
authors: Brian T. Pentland; Youngjin Yoo; Jan Recker; Inkyu Kim
rationale: Results are 10,000 simulated network trajectories (Figures 3-6). Algorithm and parameter ranges sit in Online Appendix A and Table A-1, not in the PDF; drug-discovery examples only illustrate.

title: The Aggregation–Learning Trade-off
authors: Henning Piezunka; Vikas A. Aggarwal; Hart E. Posen
rationale: Multi-agent bandit simulation; Figures 2-7 are model output. Section 3.3 gives parameters, but prejoin sampling is only "highly exploratory" and tie-breaking is unstated.

title: Division of Labor Through Self-Selection
authors: Marlo Raveendran; Phanish Puranam; Massimo Warglien
rationale: Agent-based matching model; Figures 3-4 computed over 1,000 iterations. Implementation and figures for the three contingency analyses sit in the online supplement.

title: Wisdom in the Wild: Generalization and Adaptive Dynamics
authors: Jaeho Choi; Daniel Levinthal
rationale: Computational model of category-based reinforcement learning, 25,000 runs. Figures 1 and 3-8 are numerical output. M, w, T, payoffs and update rule given. Online appendix holds robustness only.

title: When Less Is More: How Statistical Discrimination Can Decrease Predictive Accuracy
authors: Felipe A. Csaszar; Diana Jue-Rajasingh; Michael Jensen
package_where: Online appendix at https://doi.org/10.1287/orsc.2022.1626 (Mathematica notebook deriving all formulas)
rationale: Analytical lens model. Table 1 gives closed-form MSE formulas, Figures 2-5 plot them over stated parameter values. No data.

title: Reject and Resubmit: A Formal Analysis of Gender Differences in Reapplication and Their Contribution to Women’s Presence in Talent Pipelines
authors: Isabel Fernandez-Mateo; Brian Rubineau; Venkat Kuppuswamy
package_where: Journal supplement, https://doi.org/10.1287/orsc.2022.1635 (code for model, calculations, tables and figures)
rationale: Four-parameter stock-flow model solved over its parameter space; three cases only calibrate it. Figure 8 rests on a patent-class correlation from personal communication.

title: Organizational Culture, Adaptation, and Performance
authors: Francisco Brahm; Joaquin Poblete
rationale: Cultural evolution model; Figures 1-9 graph the ESS from Equations 14-16 with stated C, c, p, lambda, mu. The helping-cost function m(a) is only described as increasing and convex.

title: Conflict, Chaos, and the Art of Institutional Design
authors: Scott C. Ganz
package_where: Online supplement at https://doi.org/10.1287/orsc.2023.1662 (simulation code)
rationale: Agent-based NK model with a spatial political space; all results simulated. Parameters given (n=12, K=0/5, d, p=2/3, 4,000 landscapes, 100 periods); code in online supplement.

title: When Funders Aren’t Customers: Reputation Management and Capability Underinvestment in Multiaudience Organizations
authors: David Keith; Lauren Taylor; James Paine; Richard Weisbach; Anthony Dowidowicz
package_where: Online appendix at https://doi.org/10.1287/orsc.2022.1579 (details on running the full model and reproducing all analyses and figures)
rationale: System dynamics model of capability and reputation; results are simulated trajectories and phase plots (Figures 3-7). Fieldwork at six nonprofits only motivates the model. Equations and parameters printed.

title: Bringing Politics Back In: The Role of Power and Coalitions in Organizational Adaptation
authors: Daniel A. Levinthal; Dong Nghi Pham
rationale: NK-style agent-based model of subunits and corporate strategy (M=3, N=7, goal conflict 0 to 1). Algorithm is given, but the number of simulation runs is not stated.

title: How Does Network Structure Impact Socially Reinforced Diffusion?
authors: Jad Georges Sassine; Hazhir Rahmandad
rationale: Agent-based contagion model on ring-lattice and random networks. States, transitions and figure parameters are in the text; rewiring details and the Figure 11 boundary procedure sit in Online Appendices S4-S5.

title: The Natural Emergence of Category Effects on Rugged Landscapes
authors: Anthony Vashevko
package_where: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/os-categories-42D7 (endnote 3)
rationale: Simulated producer entry on a Brownian landscape, 1,000 markets over 250 periods. Utility parameters a and b get no values in the main text. Code is posted.

title: Learning in Temporally Complex Problems: The Role of External Knowledge
authors: Christina Fang; Ji-hyun (Jason) Kim; Hisan Yang
rationale: SARSA reinforcement learning simulation on a binary hypercube. Section 3.6 gives pseudo code and Table 2 every parameter value.

title: Cautious Exploitation: Learning and Search in Problems of Evaluation and Discovery
authors: Daniel A. Levinthal; Daniel Schliesmann
rationale: Bandit simulation with Bush-Mosteller updating and softmax choice. Beta(2,2) payoffs, N, horizon, phi and tau grids, turbulence and 10,000 environments are all stated.

title: How Capability Differences, Transaction Costs, and Learning Curves Interact to Shape Vertical Scope
authors: Michael G. Jacobides
special_software: GAMS (mixed complementarity problem solver)
rationale: Computational model solved as MCP in GAMS; equations in appendix and main parameters in Table 3, but learning and investment coefficients and firm capability draws are not printed.

title: Hoping for A to Z While Rewarding Only A: Complex Organizations and Multiple Goals
authors: Sendil K. Ethiraj; Daniel Levinthal
rationale: Adapted NK model with multiple goals; Figures 2-6 report averages over 250 replications of 250 periods. N, M, R, G and search rules are given. No empirical data.

title: Different Truths in Different Worlds
authors: Kent D. Miller; Shu-Jou Lin
rationale: Agent-based learning model in MATLAB. The grid, learning rules, dominant-coalition code and every parameter value are given in the text and Table 1.

title: A Dynamic Model of Individual and Collective Learning Amid Disruption
authors: Edward G. Anderson; Kyle Lewis
rationale: System dynamics model of individual and collective learning. Equations 1-9b and Table 1 give every base-case parameter; results are simulated trajectories in Figures 5 and 6.

title: Open Collaboration for Innovation: Principles and Performance
authors: Sheen S. Levine; Michael J. Prietula
rationale: Agent-based model; Figures 1-3 report computational experiments. Main text gives rules and some parameters, but the full algorithm, parameter table and pseudocode sit in the electronic companion.

title: Moving from an Exception to a Rule: Analyzing Mechanisms in Emergence-Based Institutionalization
authors: Jeannette A. Colyvas; Spiro Maroulis
package_where: Online appendix (NetLogo code), http://dx.doi.org/10.1287/orsc.2014.0948
special_software: NetLogo
rationale: Agent-based model of lab patenting thresholds; Figures 4-7 are simulation output. Text gives rules and most parameters but not the mutation value; code is in the online appendix.

title: Integrative Capabilities, Vertical Integration, and Innovation Over Successive Technology Lifecycles
authors: Constance E. Helfat; Miguel A. Campo-Rembado
rationale: Stylized economic analysis of integration over technology lifecycles; one inequality and graphs 'not drawn to scale', no computed or numerical results, no data.

title: The Dual Challenge of Search and Coordination for Organizational Adaptation: How Structures of Influence Matter
authors: Özgecan Koçak; Daniel A. Levinthal; Phanish Puranam
rationale: Multiagent reinforcement-learning simulation. Equations 1-4 and baseline values (N = S = 7, tau = 0.05, w, 1,000 landscapes) are in the text. No empirical data.

title: Social Institutions and Work Centrality: Explorations Beyond National Culture
authors: K. Praveen Parboteeah; John B. Cullen
sources: World Values Survey (WVS), 1990-1993 wave, as provided by ICPSR [T1, sample]; United Nations Statistical Yearbook (United Nations 1992) [T0, key_independent]; OECD Employment Outlook (1991) and Visser (1991), union density [T0, key_independent]; World Bank World Development Indicators (World Bank 1998) [T0, key_independent]; United Nations Development Program (1991) Human Development Report, educational attainment score [T0, key_independent]; Hofstede (2001) national culture scores [T0, control]
rationale: HLM of WVS 1990 respondents in 26 countries on country indicators from UN, OECD, World Bank and UNDP publications. All sources named and public.

title: Aspiration Performance and Railroads’ Patterns of Learning from Train Wrecks and Crashes
authors: Joel A. C. Baum; Kristina B. Dahlin
sources: FRA Office of Safety Analysis, Rail Equipment Accident/Incident Report [T0, sample]; American Association of Railroads (AAR) Office of Finance [T4, control]
rationale: Sample, accident costs and experience measures come from public FRA accident data. Financial and track controls were provided by the AAR.

title: Continuous Learning: The Influence of National Institutional Logics on Training Attitudes
authors: Xiaowei Luo
sources: Eurobarometer 44.0: Cancer, Education Issues, and the Single European Currency, October-November 1995 [T1, sample]; Statism and corporateness coding of countries (Schofer and Fourcade-Gourinchas 2001) [R, key_independent]; Country-level socioeconomic indicators from publications of the World Bank, ILO, OECD [T0, control]; Hofstede (2001) power distance and individualism scales [T0, robustness]; Continuous polity proxies: cultural-political individualism (Frank et al. 1995), etatism (Esping-Andersen 1990), interest-group pluralism (Lijphart 1999), OECD trade union density [T0, robustness]
rationale: Public secondary survey (Eurobarometer 44.0) analysed with hierarchical models. Country polity codes are listed in the text. No own data collection.

title: Do Cultural Differences Matter in Mergers and Acquisitions? A Tentative Model and Examination
authors: Günter K. Stahl; Andreas Voigt
sources: Published primary studies of cultural differences and M&A outcomes (effect sizes not printed) [T2, sample]; Unpublished papers and extra statistics supplied by primary-study authors; synopsis of effect sizes from first author [T4, sample]
rationale: Meta-analysis of 46 studies. Effect sizes aren't printed, some come from unpublished data sent by authors, and the synopsis is only available from the first author.

title: Organizational Learning from Extreme Performance Experience: The Impact of Success and Recovery Experience
authors: June-Young Kim; Ji-Yub (Jay) Kim; Anne S. Miner
sources: IDC Financial Publishing (bank financial data and IDC CAMEL ratings) [T2, sample]; Federal Reserve Board, Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, and FDIC [T0, dependent]; SNL Financial's Bank Regulatory Database [T2, control]; NCREIF Property Index [T2, control]; State unemployment rate, state per capita personal income, bank prime loan rate [T0, control]
rationale: Success and recovery experience are built from IDC's proprietary CAMEL ratings, bought from a commercial vendor. Every model uses them.

title: These Lives Will Not Be Lost in Vain: Organizational Learning from Disaster in U.S. Coal Mining
authors: Peter M. Madsen
sources: MSHA employment and accident/injury files [T0, sample]; Federal Register (MSHA rule changes) [T0, control]
rationale: All mine, accident and production variables come from MSHA employment and accident/injury files, 1983-2006; Table 3 adds Federal Register rule counts. Both public.

title: Certifications and Reputation: Determining the Standard of Desirability Amidst Uncertainty
authors: Scott D. Graffin; Andrew J. Ward
sources: Sean Lahman's Baseball Archive [T0, sample]; Voting for MLB's Hall of Fame by the Baseball Writers Association of America (BBWAA) [T0, dependent]; Player awards (MVP, World Series MVP, Rookie of the Year, All-Star, Gold Glove) [T0, key_independent]; Career offensive and defensive statistics, team winning percentage, World Series titles, attendance [T0, control]
rationale: Hall of Fame votes, awards and career statistics for 1,042 players are public baseball records. Lahman's Baseball Archive is named only in the acknowledgments.

title: The Dynamics of the Performance–Risk Relationship Within a Performance Period: The Moderating Role of Deadline Proximity
authors: David W. Lehman; Jungpil Hahn; Rangaraj Ramanujam; Bradley J. Alge
sources: NFL play-by-play data, regular season games 2000-2005 [T0, sample]
rationale: Every variable comes from NFL play-by-play records of 22,603 fourth-down plays, a public sports record. The paper doesn't say where the authors got the file.

title: The Liability of Leading: Battling Aspiration and Survival Goals in the Jeopardy! Tournament of Champions
authors: Elizabeth Boyle; Zur Shapira
sources: Jeopardy! Tournament of Champions records for 1990-1999, provided by the show's producers [T4, sample]; Authors' videotapes of the 2000 and 2001 Tournament of Champions broadcasts [T0, sample]
rationale: Wagers and scores for 1990-1999 were provided by the Jeopardy! producers, T4 as written; 2000-2001 came from broadcasts. J! Archive holds the same public game records.

authors: Jamal Shamsie; Michael J. Mannor

authors: Arkadiy V. Sakhartov

authors: Sungho Kim; Jaideep (Jay) Anand

authors: Hart E. Posen; Michael J. Leiblein; John S. Chen

authors: Hart E. Posen; Dirk Martignoni

authors: Mo Chen; Aseem Kaul; Brian Wu

title: Knowledge mobilization in the face of imitation: Microfoundations of knowledge aggregation and firm‐level innovation
authors: Jason P. Davis; Vikas A. Aggarwal
rationale: Computational model of knowledge mobilization under imitation; most parameters stated, but initial knowledge endowments and some imitation and recombination details are not given.

title: A contingency perspective on imitation strategies: When is “benchmarking” ineffective?
authors: Hart E. Posen; Sangyoon Yi; Jeho Lee
rationale: Agent-based imitation model. Figures 2-6 are simulation output, Table 1 gives every parameter, 1,000 runs. No empirical data. Sensitivity figures sit in the online appendix.

title: Power to the people: The benefits and limits of employee self‐selection in organizations
authors: Harsh Ketkar; Maciej Workiewicz
rationale: Agent-based model of self-selection versus centralized allocation; distributions, r=16, m values, 20 periods and 10,000 iterations stated. Code only 'available from the authors'.

authors: J. Richard Harrison; Glenn R. Carroll

authors: Sendil K. Ethiraj; Daniel Levinthal

authors: Daniel Levinthal; Hart E. Posen

Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD) [T0, control]; Polity IV [T0, control]

title: State Agency Discretion and Entrepreneurship in Regulated Markets
authors: Jake B. Grandy; Shon R. Hiatt

authors: Nathan Wilmers

authors: Alex Vestal; Erwin Danneels

title: Calling and the Good Life: A Meta-Analysis and Theoretical Extension
authors: Shoshana R. Dobrow; Hannah Weisman; Daniel Heller; Jennifer Tosti-Kharas

title: From Chaos to Systems: The Engineering Foundations of Organization Theory, 1879-1932
authors: Yehouda Shenhav

title: Collaborative Brokerage, Generative Creativity, and Creative Success
authors: Lee Fleming; Santiago Mingo; David Chen

rationale: Every variable is built from USPTO utility patent records with the authors' inventor-matching algorithm (Appendix A); no survey or proprietary source.

authors: Gino Cattani; Simone Ferriani; Giacomo Negro; Fabrizio Perretti

Fetrow (1999) filmography of 1950s U.S. feature films [T2, sample]; Motion Picture Catalog of the Library of Congress (copyright entries 1950-1959) [T0, sample]; The Motion Picture Guide 1927-1982 (Nash and Ross, Cinebooks) [T2, sample]; The Motion Picture Year Book and the Motion Picture Almanac (industry-level statistics) [T2, control]; Historical Statistics of the United States, Colonial Times to 1970 (recreational expenditures) [T0, robustness]

title: Board Composition: Balancing Family Influence in S&P 500 Firms
authors: Ronald C. Anderson; David M. Reeb

title: Vive La Résistance: Competing Logics and the Consolidation of U.S. Community Banking
